entries.name: Family and consumer sciences
entries.definition: The field that studies how individuals and families manage daily life, including nutrition, child development, household finance and textiles; historically called home economics.

entries.name: Family engagement
entries.definition: Involving the families of children or clients in their education, care or services through communication and partnership.

entries.name: Family ministry
entries.definition: The programmes, teaching and pastoral care a church provides for families.

entries.name: Family systems theory
entries.definition: A framework in psychology and family therapy that treats the family as an emotional system whose members' behaviour is understood through their relationships; Murray Bowen developed it most fully.

entries.name: Farm implements
entries.definition: Equipment pulled or powered by a tractor to work the land and crops, such as ploughs, harrows, seeders and mowers.

entries.name: Farm management
entries.definition: Planning and running a farm as a business, including crops, livestock, labour, equipment and finances.

entries.name: FAS 109
entries.definition: A US accounting standard (FASB Statement No. 109) on how to account for income taxes, now part of ASC Topic 740.

entries.name: FAST ESP
entries.definition: An enterprise search platform from FAST Search & Transfer, later part of Microsoft, for indexing and searching large collections of content.

entries.name: fastai
entries.definition: A Python deep-learning library built on PyTorch, from the fast.ai research group, that gives high-level components for training neural networks.

entries.name: Feminist theory
entries.definition: A body of scholarship that examines gender inequality and women's experience, drawing on many academic fields.

entries.name: FGDC Standards
entries.definition: Geospatial data standards, such as metadata standards, endorsed by the US Federal Geographic Data Committee.

entries.name: Fibre Channel
entries.definition: A high-speed networking technology, standardised by INCITS, used mainly to connect servers to storage area networks.

entries.name: Field-programmable gate array
entries.definition: An integrated circuit whose logic can be configured after manufacture, using a hardware description language, to implement custom digital circuits.

entries.name: FigJam
entries.definition: Figma's online whiteboard for brainstorming, diagramming and planning with a team.

entries.name: File control block
entries.definition: A data structure in an operating system or file system that holds the information needed to manage an open file.

entries.name: Filleting
entries.definition: Cutting the flesh from the bones of fish or meat to produce boneless fillets.

entries.name: Film scoring
entries.definition: Composing and arranging original music to accompany a film or video.

entries.name: Finacle
entries.definition: Infosys's suite of core banking and digital banking software for banks.

entries.name: Final expense insurance
entries.definition: A small whole-life insurance policy meant to pay for funeral, burial and other end-of-life costs.

entries.name: Finance automation
entries.definition: Using software, workflows and scripts to carry out finance tasks such as reconciliations, payables and reporting with little manual work.

entries.name: Finance software
entries.definition: Software used to manage money and financial records, such as accounting, budgeting, treasury and reporting systems.

entries.name: Financial acumen
entries.definition: Understanding how money, financial statements and financial decisions work, and using that understanding to make sound business choices.

entries.name: Financial analytics
entries.definition: Analysing financial data, such as revenue, costs and risk, with statistical and data tools to support decisions.

entries.name: Financial consolidation
entries.definition: Combining the financial statements of a parent company and its subsidiaries into a single set of group accounts.

entries.name: Financial forecasting
entries.definition: Estimating future revenue, costs and cash flow from past results and assumptions.

entries.name: Financial Information eXchange
entries.definition: A messaging standard used to exchange securities trades and market data electronically between financial firms.

entries.name: Financial privacy
entries.definition: Protecting people's personal financial information and following the rules on how it may be collected, shared and used.

entries.name: Financial risk management
entries.definition: Identifying, measuring and controlling financial risks such as market, credit and liquidity risk.

entries.name: FINCAD
entries.definition: Financial analytics software for valuing and managing derivatives and other complex financial instruments.

entries.name: FinCEN 314 program
entries.definition: The information-sharing rules under Section 314 of the USA PATRIOT Act, run by FinCEN, that let law enforcement and financial institutions share information about suspected money laundering and terrorist financing.

entries.name: Model fine-tuning
entries.definition: Adapting model parameters to selected tasks or examples.

entries.name: Firebase Cloud Messaging
entries.definition: Google's cloud service for sending push notifications and messages to Android, iOS and web apps.

entries.name: First article inspection
entries.definition: A documented check that the first part made from a new design or process meets all drawing and specification requirements.

entries.name: FIS GetPaid
entries.definition: FIS's software for managing accounts receivable, credit and collections.

entries.name: Flask
entries.definition: A lightweight Python web framework for building web applications and APIs.

entries.name: Flat sketching
entries.definition: Drawing flat, two-dimensional technical drawings of garments that show seams, stitching and proportions for design and production.

entries.name: Flatbed truck
entries.definition: A truck with an open, flat cargo bed and no sides or roof, used to haul large or irregular loads.

entries.name: Flavor development
entries.definition: Creating and refining flavours for food and drink products.

entries.name: Flexible Single Master Operations
entries.definition: The specialised domain controller roles in Microsoft Active Directory that only one server at a time may hold, such as schema master and PDC emulator.

entries.name: FlexiSIGN
entries.definition: Sign-making and large-format print design software, from Scanvec Amiable, used to design signs and drive cutters and printers.
